diagnostic_evidence.quote: For typical choices of the spatial kernel such as Gaussian RBF, this decay is exponential in $m$

issues.failure_explanation: The introduction promises a bound ||mu - mu_hat||^2 <= O(m exp(-alpha m^{1/d})) that depends on m only. The only stated guarantee is (eigenbound). It carries an explicit factor n/S and the tail of the eigenvalues of the n x n Gram matrix K_XX, which themselves grow with n. It also carries an unspecified weight-dependent constant C, holds only with probability 1-3delta, and uses m ~ S log(S/delta), so S ~ m/log m rather than m. No argument converts this into the advertised m-only rate. The text after the theorem then calls the decay 'exponential in m', which contradicts the m^{1/d} (stretched-exponential, d=3) form claimed earlier.

failure_location.quote: automatically carry over to the normal-cycles setting

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the guarantee as the eigenvalue-tail bound actually proved. Alternatively, add a lemma bounding Gaussian Gram-matrix eigenvalues on bounded point sets, giving an explicit rate with its n- and weight-dependent prefactor, log factors and failure probability. Replace 'exponential in m' by the stretched-exponential form.
issues.overall_effect: The headline rate guarantee in the contribution section, and the 'exponential in m' claim, are unsupported. What is established is a probabilistic, n-dependent eigenvalue-tail bound.
issues.title: Advertised n-free (stretched-)exponential error rate does not follow from the stated eigenvalue bound
issues.why_classification: The method and the eigenvalue-tail guarantee survive. Recovering a rate statement needs a contained additional lemma and a weaker, n-dependent advertised bound, so the loss is limited rather than major.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: so that $S_{a,b}^{+,\perp}$ is a half circle in the plane perpendicular to $a$

issues.failure_explanation: (i) For the unit half circle defined in the source, the arc-length integral of u is 2*beta_T, not (pi/2)*beta_T. The cylindrical coefficient is therefore miscomputed. (ii) The component formulas give coefficient -pi/2 for the cylindrical part and -pi for the spherical part. The spherical sign also conflicts with the all-plus signs in (boundarysph). (NC_delta) instead uses pi for both parts. (realembedding) uses pi for the edge part and pi/2 for the boundary part, and places the edge deltas at x_i rather than at the edge centres c_i. (iii) With the spherical coefficient pi, the boundary term of the inner product is pi^2 <A_i,B_j>, not the pi^2/4 of (NC_disc_met); with NC_delta's coefficients both terms get pi^2. So the asserted agreement with thm:added-1 fails for every version given. The relative weighting of the edge and boundary terms, which is not a global scale, differs between versions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the half-circle and hemisphere integrals and the orientation signs consistently (cylindrical factor 2, spherical factor pi). Place the edge deltas at the edge centres. Propagate the same constants into NC_delta and realembedding, and reconcile or correct the stated comparison with thm:added-1.
issues.overall_effect: The Dirac representation that is embedded and compressed is not shown to equal (or approximate) N(T) with the correct relative edge/boundary weights. The claimed consistency with the cited closed-form metric fails, and so does the identification of the compressed object with the normal-cycle metric.
issues.title: Dirac delta weights of the normal cycle carry wrong and mutually inconsistent constants
issues.why_classification: The compression guarantee is weight-agnostic, so the method survives. However, the central representation needs a consistent re-derivation, and the claimed agreement with the cited formula must be corrected or withdrawn. The relative boundary weighting changes the metric, so this is more than a forced typo fix.

issues.failure_explanation: The hypothesis concerns mu_S with weights alpha_i. Both conclusions (tracebound, eigenbound) bound the distance from sum delta_{x_i} alpha_hat_i, but alpha_hat_i is never defined. As stated, the theorem therefore does not bound ||mu_S - mu_hat||. The constant C is also unspecified. Since the left side scales quadratically in the weights while tr(K_XX - Q_XX) does not, C must depend on alpha (e.g. ||alpha||_F^2); with an absolute constant the bound is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace alpha_hat_i by alpha_i and state C explicitly, e.g. C = sum_i ||alpha_i||^2, which follows from ||mu - P mu||^2 = tr(alpha^T (K_XX - Q_XX) alpha).
issues.overall_effect: The formal guarantee for Algorithm FunctionalCompressionAlg, as written, is not about the target functional, and its constant is ill-specified.
issues.title: Compression theorem bounds an undefined functional with an unspecified constant
issues.why_classification: A short, standard local correction restores the intended bound with no change to the method, rate or scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which is a consistent approximation \cite{NCpaper}, as the edge-lengths tend to zero.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper's guarantee (thm:added-3) bounds only the distance between the compressed functional and the discrete Dirac form. That form is obtained by replacing each cylindrical current by an edge-centre quadrature, yet it is written as an exact equality N(T) = ... in (NC_delta). Its error relative to N(T), and N(T)'s error relative to the smooth shape, are cited only as qualitative consistency, with no rate. No bound on the distance to the true shape's normal cycle is established.

failure_location.quote: guarantees of small RKHS distance to the normal cycle of the true underlying shape

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claim to the discrete (edge-centre-approximated) normal cycle and mark NC_delta as an approximation. Alternatively, add a quantified discretisation bound and combine it via the triangle inequality.
issues.overall_effect: The concluding guarantee overstates the results: only compression error relative to the discretised Dirac representation is controlled.
issues.title: Conclusion claims guarantees relative to the true shape's normal cycle
issues.why_classification: The fix withdraws an advertised guarantee type, distance to the true shape, but leaves a recognisably comparable result for the discrete normal cycle. This is a limited weakening, not a major loss.
